- When sentiment turns negative or shows sharp decline, model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast dip by 5–10% relative to prior low.
- After strong upward sentiment spikes, model often overshoots — cap forecast at 1.5x recent high or 20% above prior peak.
- If sentiment remains flat or weak for 3+ days, model overestimates mean reversion — adjust downward by 2–5% per day of flat sentiment.
- When news volume drops to 0 for 2+ consecutive days, model underreacts — increase forecast by 3–7% to account for lagged market adjustment.
- If model forecast is consistently 5–10% above true outcome over 3+ consecutive days, apply downward bias correction of 1–2% per day.
- If sentiment change is positive but model forecast is flat or declining, model underestimates momentum — increase forecast by 2–5% to match sentiment momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates volatility in high-sentiment periods — add 1–3% buffer to forecast if sentiment > 0.67 for 5+ days.
